The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x+1)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x+1)) \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}-(-\frac{1}{(2x+1)\sqrt{1-(2x+1)^{2}}})\cdot (2x+1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{(2x+1)\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}-4x-1}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}+\frac{2}{(2x+1)\sqrt{-4{x}^{2}-4x}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{-4x(x+1)}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}(1+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{-x(x+1)}}).\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)+\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(x-1)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(x-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{1-(x-1)^{2}}\cdot (x-1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{1-({x}^{2}-2x+1)}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{2x-{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}-\frac{1}{x(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}(1-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{x-1}{x(x-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & ={(x+2)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+(x+2)\cdot {(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x\,+\,(x+2)\cdot (\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+\frac{x+2}{1-{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
